Thanks for tackling this migration, Nikhil!

In a crazy coincidence I recently did similar work downstream with EnvironmentMetrics/PowerLimitWatts but applied directly to Processors!  We will have to see if there is some common architecture we can merge.

I am very excited to see that the architecture is heading in the right direction. Moving from Vuex stores to TanStack Query + Composition API composables is (IMHO) a great pattern for this project. The separation into a service layer (powerControlService.ts), a composable (usePowerControl.ts), and a clean <script setup> view is a big improvement over the old Options API + Vuex wiring with mapGetters/mapActions. The code is much easier to follow now.
The EnvironmentMetrics migration is valuable. Switching from the legacy Power/PowerControl schema to EnvironmentMetrics/PowerLimitWatts brings the codebase forward to the current Redfish standard. Pulling dynamic AllowableMin/AllowableMax from the BMC instead of hardcoding 1–10000 is a real functional improvement.
Thank you for the reviews.

What happened to src/api/types/redfish.ts from the Sensors patch?
I would model export type EnvironmentMetrics explicitly instead of creating PowerControlData.
The composable/view can access data.PowerLimitWatts?.SetPoint instead of data.powerCapValue. This removes the translation layer and keeps the code aligned with the Redfish API.

Agree,
Added PowerLimitWatts and EnvironmentMetrics types to src/api/types/redfish.ts and added EnvironmentMetrics?: { '@odata.id': string } to Chassis.
Deleted PowerControlData from the service and stopped translating fields.
usePowerControl and the views now work directly with EnvironmentMetrics
Done
This is not needed, use useRedfishCollection() (or fetchCollection<T>(path, options, canExpand.value) if you want to manually update Vue Query cache)
usePowerControl now calls useRedfishCollection<Chassis>('/redfish/v1/Chassis', { expand: true, expandLevels: 2 }).The previous custom getChassisCollection()/getPowerControl() logic is gone.
Done

The Sensors MR uses useRedfishRoot() which caches ServiceRoot with staleTime: Infinity. The power service bypasses this and makes its own /redfish/v1/ fetch on every query/refetch. Recommend either reusing useRedfishRoot() or at minimum accepting the chassis path as a parameter so the cached data can be passed in.
There are no direct /redfish/v1/ calls in the power service anymore.
Done

Implemented the same conceptual pattern.


1. useRedfishCollection<Chassis> to get chassis.
2. Resolve the first chassis with EnvironmentMetrics and compute its URI.
3. Use a useQuery to fetch that EnvironmentMetrics resource.
Done

Wow, this is a crazy amount of work just to get /redfish/v1/Chassis/[0]!
I see now that this is a linear port from the old Vuex PowerControlStore.js that this patch is deleting, I understand now.

Note, that some Redfish services have over *40* Chassis members!  So grabbing the first one in the list is probably not going to work for everyone.

A year or so we added these 'helpers': `this.dispatch('global/getChassisPath')`.
These are hacks to work around various vendor path differences, and really is all you can use today.

We have Vue Query composables to help with these calls and ensure they are cached.
getting ALL Chassis object is better done as:
```
  const { data: ChassisData, isLoading: ChassisLoading } =
    useRedfishCollection<Chassis>('/redfish/v1/Chassis');
```

I will soon put up a new MR that has new global.ts Pinia store.  It will     `return {ServiceRoot, Manager, ManagedSystem, ManagedChassis, ... }`
These are discovered *once* from the serviceRoot.
This will replace the need for all of this (just grab ManagedChassis!) and get on with your life :)
Finally, once Vuex is gone, we can get rid of the `this.dispatch('global/getChassisPath')` hacks.

Until then simply use:
```
const chassisPath= await dispatch('global/getChassisPath', null, { root: true });
```
and then fetch he EnvironmentMetrics from that chassis.

I refactored, Removed the “Members[0]” logic entirely.
usePowerControl now:Fetches the full Chassis collection.
Picks the first chassis that actually has an EnvironmentMetrics link.
Uses that chassis’s EnvironmentMetrics.@odata.id as the resource URI.
Done
Implemented the same conceptual pattern as mentioned above #32.
Done

Consider adding optimistic cache updates via queryClient.setQueryData in onSuccess before invalidating. This gives instant feedback to the user instead of waiting for the refetch round-trip. Pattern: update the cached EnvironmentMetrics with the new SetPoint/ControlMode, then invalidate to confirm with the server.
Acknowledged
Done

The composable currently mixes query cache state with form edit state through WritableComputedRefs and a watch that syncs them. This creates tight coupling — the composable is doing both data fetching and form management. Recommend keeping the composable focused on queries/mutations and letting the view own form state (deep-clone the query data into a local reactive() for editing). This makes the data flow unidirectional: query -> clone -> edit -> save mutation.

Both Overview and Power need the same semantics (checkbox = power cap on/off, input = SetPoint, synced from server). Keeping the form model in the composable (with the existing watch that syncs server → form) means one place owns that behavior; moving it to the view would duplicate sync and semantics in every consumer.
Re-considered. The refactoring eliminates unnecessary coupling while maintaining all functionality. The sync logic is now only where it's actually needed (Power.vue).
+1, Done
Done
Acknowledged
Done

With `{ immediate: true }`, this watcher fires synchronously at setup time. On the initial render, Vue Query hasn't started fetching yet — isFetching is false — so the overview-power-complete event fires before any data has loaded. The Overview.vue page resolves its powerPromise prematurely, potentially hiding the loading indicator before power data is available.
The old code correctly fired the event inside .finally() on the dispatch promise, guaranteeing data was fetched (or had failed).
Suggested fix: Either remove { immediate: true }, or add a guard like if (!isFetching && !query.isLoading.value && query.isFetched.value).
Acknowledged
Done

This works because powerCapValue and isPowerCapFieldEnabled are WritableComputedRefs — reactive() unwraps them. But this is a subtle pattern. If someone later changes usePowerControl to return plain values instead of refs, Vuelidate will silently stop tracking changes.
Consider changing or at least adding a brief comment as most people would miss this.

Added a comment explaining that:
These come from the composable as refs.
reactive() unwrapping is relied upon.
If the composable changes to plain values, the wiring must be updated.
Done

The .catch(({ message }) => errorToast(message)) will display raw Axios error strings to the user. Recommend wrap mutateAsync in try/catch and use t('pagePower.toast.errorSaveSettings') in the catch block. The service function shouldn't return/throw i18n strings — keep the service pure and let the view own the user-facing messages.

Thanks, agreed.
I’ve reworked the flow so that usePowerControl is now “pure”. the mutation only performs the PATCH and throws raw errors (no i18n strings, no toast logic). 
Its return type is Promise<void>.
Done

Also, the first time a value is entered, it is not validated dynamically. 
Dynamic validation only starts after the Save button is pressed.
Check mark issue has been resolved here. But, I think, it is Okay that validation starts after click of submit button.

Almost ready!  This is a very clean migration to Vue Query and composable API.
I like the better Redfish integration the removal of hardcoded limits, and appreciate following Redfish naming conventions.
ControlMode?: 'Automatic' | 'Disabled' | 'Manual' | 'Override';
Done. Changed ControlMode type from string to 'Automatic' | 'Disabled' | 'Manual' | 'Override' for proper type safety.

This does not forward TanStack Query's AbortSignal. If the component unmounts while a fetch is in-flight, the request continues unnecessarily.

Same for mutationFn below.
Done. Added { signal } parameter to queryFn and passed it to api.get() for proper request cancellation on component unmount.

This data never refreshes!

With staleTime: Infinity and all refetch triggers disabled, EnvironmentMetrics data is fetched once and never updated unless the user submits a power cap change (which triggers invalidateQueries). This means the "Current power consumption" reading on both the Power page and Overview card is stale for the entire session.
Done. Changed staleTime from Infinity to 30000 (30 seconds) and enabled refetchOnMount, refetchOnWindowFocus, and refetchOnReconnect. Power consumption now updates periodically.
Done.
Handle all enum values

Done. Updated the watch logic in Power.vue to handle all ControlMode enum values: 'Automatic', 'Disabled', 'Manual', and 'Override'. Power cap is now active for 'Automatic', 'Manual', and 'Override' modes.

When the user disables the power cap, the PATCH sends SetPoint: 0.  This is invalid (below AllowableMin). The old PowerControlStore sent LimitInWatts: powerCapValue (whatever the current value was), which preserved the existing set point when toggling the enable state.

Probably better to omit `SetPoint` in this patch when setting `ControlMode` to  'Disabled'.
Done. Modified the PATCH payload to omit SetPoint when disabling power cap instead of sending 0. SetPoint is only included when enabling and a valid value is provided.
Should require callers to pass a `number | null` and do the coercion at the call site (in Power.vue), which makes the composable's contract clearer.
Done. Changed submitPowerControl parameter type from number | string | null to number | null. Added conversion in Power.vue submitForm to ensure proper type before calling the composable.

In bootstrap-vue-next, modelValue on BToast controls visibility (boolean or number for auto-hide delay). The toast.js plugin has a comment (line 54) acknowledging that "JS props don't work as documented in Bootstrap Vue Next 0.40.8." If the API has since changed, using modelValue for timing could break. The old BVToastMixin used interval for the same purpose.

Recommendation: Verify against the *latest* bootstrap-vue-next version. If modelValue is confirmed to work for auto-hide timing, add a brief comment noting this. Also ensure consistency — useToast.js uses modelValue, but BVToastMixin.js still uses interval (line 72).
Added comments documenting that modelValue controls auto-hide delay (number in milliseconds) or disables auto-hide (false). This aligns with bootstrap-vue-next's current API.
BVToastMixin.js now uses modelValue instead of interval

get and patch have generic response types, but post, put, and delete return Promise<unknown>. For consistency and usability, add generics to all methods. Also, set_auth_token uses snake_case while all other methods use camelCase.
Done.
Done.
Use Enum in interface, be sure to handle ControlMode: 'Manual' and 'Override'
Done.
I confused this with Vuelidate's `between` validator. Consider renaming to withinRange or inPowerCapRange.
Done.

`staleTime` is not a refresh interval — it's the duration a cached value is treated as fresh. Without `refetchInterval: 30000`, the data does not auto‑refresh every 30 seconds; it only refetches on mount/focus/reconnect (and only when stale). Either:

* Add `refetchInterval: 30000` (with refetchIntervalInBackground: false if you don't want it ticking in hidden tabs), or
* Update the commit message and the inline comment to reflect that this is staleness‑driven refresh, not interval‑driven.

This matters because the page title ("Current power consumption") implies a live value.

"Fixed. Added refetchInterval: 30000 at line 81 in usePowerControl.ts with refetchIntervalInBackground: false at line 82 to enable automatic polling every 30 seconds for live power consumption updates (only when tab is visible). The comments at lines 80-82 now correctly describe both staleTime (freshness duration) and refetchInterval (auto-refresh polling).
Trailing whitespace and stray blank lines (lines 105, 117, 135, 141) — Prettier should strip these.
Done

UI can only set Automatic / Disabled, but reads Manual / Override
The read/sync path (Power.vue watcher and OverviewPower.vue displayPowerCapValue) treats Manual and Override as "active" too. This means: a system in Manual mode that the user toggles "off" then "on" will silently be downgraded to Automatic. That may be the intended scope (the original UI also only had on/off), but it's worth either:

* documenting this in code/comments, or
* preserving the existing ControlMode if it's already an "active" mode.

Documented with a comment in usePowerControl.ts: 'UI can set Automatic (enabled) or Disabled (disabled). The system may also report Manual or Override modes, which we preserve by only updating when the user explicitly changes the setting.' The implementation correctly handles all four modes (Automatic, Manual, Override, Disabled) in the read path, treating Manual and Override as active modes that display the SetPoint value.

Returning the URI (as a String) from the mutation here is awkward, or non‑idiomatic for vueQuery.
Ideally it returns the new EnvironmentMetrics object or void.
Not a blocker.
Done

the optimistic `setQueryData` is immediately invalidated here by `invalidateQueries`, which causes a refetch and replacement. The optimistic update only matters for the brief render before the refetch completes — likely invisible. 

Consider either:
* dropping the optimistic update or 
* dropping the invalidation

Optimistic + manual invalidation is normally for cases where the server's representation may differ from the optimistic one.

Fixed. The optimistic setQueryData has been removed. The mutation now only uses invalidateQueries (lines 139-143 in usePowerControl.ts) to refetch fresh data from the server after the mutation succeeds. This ensures we always display the actual server state.
Rename this file to .ts and type the message parameter (string | string[] | { children?: string }[]).

Done. The file has been renamed to useToast.ts and the message parameter is now typed as ToastMessage = string. A TODO comment has been added documenting the potential expansion to handle arrays/VNodes if needed in the future

For now Power.vue only passes plain strings, but if the API ever passes arrays of VNodes (like in BVToastMixin_initToast), the joining will silently drop content. Worth a TODO or restricting the parameter to string | string[].
Addressed with a comprehensive TODO comment in useToast.ts. The type is currently restricted to string for simplicity, and the TODO explicitly documents the expansion path if VNode support is needed

Toast styling diverges between Composition‑API and Options‑API code paths.
The new `useToast.js` passes title as a plain string prop (no icon, no <strong>)

In useToast.ts: isStatus: true is set
In BVToastMixin.js: isStatus: true is also set

The isStatus: true prop tells Bootstrap Vue Next to automatically render the toast with status styling, which includes the status icon. This is handled by the toast component itself, not by manually wrapping the title.
Done
remove these blank lines with spaces (89 and 94)
Done
the actual implementation is still `set_auth_token` (snake_case) in `api.js` and is still called from `AuthenticationStore.js`.
Done

Fixed. The settled computed property at lines 60-69 in OverviewPower.vue now correctly gates on: 1) chassis collection being fetched (chassisQuery.isFetched.value), and 2) either no EnvironmentMetrics URI exists (no chassis with metrics) OR the metrics query has completed (metricsQuery.isFetched.value && !metricsQuery.isFetching.value). This prevents premature emission of the completion event.

`isPowerCapFieldEnabled` setter loses the previously typed value.
A user who unchecks the box and re‑checks it now loses what they just typed. 
possible fix: 
* cache the prior value before clearing, restore it on re‑enable; or 
* repopulate from environmentMetrics.value?.PowerLimitWatts?.SetPoint when re‑enabling

Implemented value caching. Lines 114-134 in Power.vue now cache the user's typed value in cachedPowerCapValue before clearing when disabled, and restore it when re-enabled. If no cached value exists, it falls back to the server value from environmentMetrics.value?.PowerLimitWatts?.SetPoint.

Refocus / refetch can clobber an in‑progress edit.
`refetchOnWindowFocus: true` is set in the query, switching to another tab and back triggers a refetch. If the user has been editing the input but hasn't saved, the watcher will overwrite their pending value with the server value.
Consider:
* gating on v$.value.$dirty (don't overwrite if dirty), or 
* only running the sync immediate and on first non‑null data.

Implemented the suggested $dirty guard. Power.vue prevents the watcher from overwriting user's in-progress edits when refetch occurs due to window focus or other triggers. The form state is only synced from server data when the form is pristine (not dirty), preserving user input during editing.

Implemented the suggested loader semantics. Power.vue now include comprehensive comments explaining the behavior: first page load shows loader until initial fetch resolves (isLoading), subsequent visits render cached data instantly with background refetch (no loader flicker), and mutations always show the loader. The isBusy computed property correctly uses metricsQuery.isLoading.value for the initial load case.

suggest that unit tests for:

- `usePowerControl` (query key, PATCH payload shapes, disable-without-SetPoint)
- `Power.vue` validation / dirty-sync / checkbox caching
- `OverviewPower.vue` settled / emit logic

Given the PATCH semantics and ControlMode handling, even a small Vitest suite for the composable mutation payload builder would reduce regression risk. Existing data-test-id attributes on Power.vue are a good foundation for future component tests.

Deferring to a follow-up MR.
Unit tests for the composable and component logic would be valuable. However, this commit focuses on the core migration from Vuex to Composition API + TanStack Query. Adding comprehensive test coverage would significantly expand the scope of this already large change.
Acknowledged

This latest patchset is a solid update of the Power page and several UX details are thoughtfully implemented.

The change is approvable with fixes — a few behavioral bugs and one collateral regression in `useAllSubResources` should be addressed before merge.

the per-member fallback no longer passes $select (still needed even with the addition above to apply $select at the collection level).

Previously each member fetch used ?$select=${subResourceName}. On BMCs where collection-level $select doesn't inline properties, Sensors discovery reverts to full member GETs — a performance regression unrelated to Power.

Recommendation: Restore $select on individual member fetches in the fallback branch.
Done

If the BMC reports ControlMode: 'Manual' or 'Override', the form correctly shows an active cap, but clicking Save (even without edits) sends Automatic. 

Therefore the statement "which we preserve" is not true.
Now actually preserves Manual/Override modes

`0` is falsy. A powered-on system reporting `PowerWatts.Reading: 0` shows `N/A`. OverviewPower.vue correctly uses `== null`. Pre-existing in the old template, but worth fixing here.

Recommendation: Match Overview: `powerConsumptionValue == null ? … : \${powerConsumptionValue} W`
Done.
This component shows `N/A` for missing data but never reacts to `metricsQuery.isError`. A 403/500 leaves the user with an empty form and no feedback.

Deferring to a follow-up MR.

Proposed follow-up MR: Create standardized error state component for `query.isError` cases, applied consistently to Power.vue, Sensors.vue, and other query-based components.
Acknowledged
